newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says revenue seen lower than targeted.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says revenue seen lower than targeted.

text.p: Acting Thai Finance Minister Chaiyawat Wibulsawat said on Wednesday that government revenue in the 1996/97 fiscal year was expected to be 16 billion baht lower than earlier projections.
Chaiyawat cited the sluggish economy as the major reason for the anticipated fall in government revenue this year.
"The preliminary estimates showed that the government's revenue would be 16 billion baht lower than previously projected," Chaiyawat told a news conference.
Thailand had projected a revenue of 984 billion baht ($39.36 billion) for the 1996/97 financial year.
"The slow economy has significantly affected the government's tax collection," he said.

But Thailand's moves to boost revenue from other sources and to curb spending on low priority projects would help the government achieve a budget surplus in the current financial year, Chaiyawat said.
"The finance ministry will continue adopting a tight fiscal policy to ensure that we still post a budget surplus this year similar to those in the past eight years," he said.
Thailand has registered a budget surplus in each of the past eight years.
Chaiyawat said government revenue could rise if the slowing Thai economy picked up later in the financial year ending September 30, 1997.
